correctness.rationale: The irredundant facets are the two terminal coordinate facets and all cover equalities. Disjoint Euclidean order simplices have volume 1/(2n)! and exact boundary-face Gram determinants 1 or 2. A Dyck word has precisely 2n minus twice its peaks plus its hills in cover-adjacent positions. Narayana symmetry and Catalan convolution yield mean n; indexed Catalan convolution determines each vertical facet area. Stirling asymptotics yield the bulk and endpoint laws. The standalone exact checker enumerated 23,713 Dyck words and confirmed 414 facet Gram determinants, corroborating but not substituting the all-n proof.

A nearby surface-area formula for rooted-tree order polytopes does not cover two-row grids whose cover graph has four-cycles. The general canonical triangulation alone requires the nontrivial hill-count calculation to reach the stated spectrum. Priority remains provisional for unindexed equivalent sources.

value.rationale: The full Euclidean vertical-facet area law is a natural coordinate-intrinsic boundary invariant for the classical two-row ladder polytope. It exposes a sharp U-shaped spatial distribution, two endpoint regimes each capturing asymptotically half the vertical-family area, a central n^{-3/2} scale, and a universal K^{-1/2} tail. This goes beyond facet count, reparameterization, or known aggregate lattice boundary coefficients and is relevant to nonuniform facet-area sampling.
